pages.title: OpenVibe.VIP
pages.summary: Memberships at openvibe.vip: creator plans, perks and benefits recognised across every OpenVibe site, with subscriptions and entitlements held by OpenVibe.Billing.
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.VIP** is the membership product at `openvibe.vip`. A creator publishes a plan, a member joins it through [[OpenVibe.Billing]], and every OpenVibe product can ask VIP whether a person is a member and may see a members-only resource.

## What it does

- **Tiers.** A creator sells up to ten tiers, one plan each, at the monthly price they set; Billing keeps and charges the price. A member holds one tier of a creator at a time.
- **Plans with fixed terms.** Every edit of a plan is a new, immutable version, and a membership always points at the version it was bought under. Plans carry no price: Billing sets and charges it.
- **Perks** such as badges, emotes, members-only content, rooms and roles, bound to the products that show them.
- **Members-only resources.** A product registers a resource as being for a creator's members, and VIP answers whether a person may see it.
- **Membership checks for anyone's software.** An app or tool where a person signed in with OpenVibe can ask VIP, with that person's token, whether they are a member; an expired, unknown or unreachable answer is always no.
- **Cards and badges** that other sites can embed.

## How it fits the network

- [[OpenVibe.Billing]] holds subscriptions and entitlements; VIP holds plans and perks.
- [[OpenVibe.Community]], [[OpenVibe.Blog]], [[OpenVibe.Chat]] and [[OpenVibe.Wiki]] use VIP for members-only content.
- Identities come from [[OpenVibe.Network]].

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha". VIP launched at openvibe.vip on 2026-10-17 with checkout open, right after Billing became the money ledger, and creators could sell tiers the same day. A channel page on OpenVibe.Live lists a creator's higher tiers next to its Subscribe button.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Zone
pages.summary: Private S3-compatible storage zones for OpenVibe projects at openvibe.zone: named buckets per project environment, scoped access keys and quotas, with the objects kept by OpenVibe.Media.
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Zone** gives every OpenVibe project private storage zones at `openvibe.zone`. A zone is an S3 bucket of one project environment, sandbox or production.

## What it does

- **Default zones.** Each environment has a default zone, which holds its existing objects.
- **Named zones.** A project creates more zones by name, each with an optional quota.
- **Names are never reused.** A zone's name is never given to another zone, even after it is deleted, so a URL signed for one bucket can never reach a different one.
- **Access keys** read, write or both. A key can be limited to some zones, and its secret is shown once.
- **S3 tools.** The AWS SDKs, rclone and backup tools reach zones over S3, path style.
- **Large files and copies.** Multipart uploads carry big objects in parts, and server-side copies (CopyObject and UploadPartCopy) move data between zones without downloading it.
- **Usage.** Requests, egress and stored bytes are counted per zone by the hour. The console shows each zone's month so far, and the project's usage page adds them up.
- **Deletion.** Deleting a zone removes every object and every copy of it. A zone holding an object under a retention hold cannot be deleted.

## How it fits the network

- **Zone owns** the zone records and their control API.
- **[[OpenVibe.Media]] owns** what is inside a zone: the objects, their bytes and copies, the S3 surface, the access keys, quota enforcement and the one deletion path. Every object in a zone is an ordinary Media object, reachable through Media's own API too.
- Projects and roles come from [[OpenVibe.Network]].
- [[OpenVibe.Services]] lists zones beside a project's other resources and can delete one.

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha". Multipart uploads, server-side copies and per-zone usage were added on 2026-10-15. The S3 endpoint is `s3.openvibe.media`, and the control API also answers at `api.openvibe.zone`.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Node
pages.summary: One service for a person's computers, servers, Raspberry Pis, phones and robots: pair it once and OpenVibe.Bot and OpenVibe.Actor can use the device, with a local kill switch.
pages.body:
**OpenVibe Node** runs on a person's own devices: computers, servers, Raspberry Pis, phones and robots. Paired once with OpenVibe, it lets products such as [[OpenVibe.Bot]] and [[OpenVibe.Actor]] use the device.

## What it does

- **The core** is one static Go binary per platform.
  - It connects out over one WebSocket and needs no open ports.
  - It keeps heartbeats, a deadman and a persisted emergency stop, and owner limits are clamped before any driver sees a value.
  - It publishes video over WHIP.
  - It installs as a system service on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **Plugins** run as separate processes: robot drivers (Adeept, Cozmo, ROS 2, and the community's LOOI driver) and the computer plugin. Every plugin stops its own actuators when its link goes quiet.
- **The computer plugin** lets an AI agent work on the machine only at the level its owner sets:
  - reading the screen;
  - files;
  - a terminal;
  - the mouse and keyboard;
  - a browser of the agent's own, in its own profile.

  At the "ask" level, each action waits for the owner's approval on the machine. The owner can answer from the tray
  (`openvibe-node tray`, on Linux and Windows), from a notification's Approve and Deny buttons, from a dialog on macOS,
  or from the command line. An approval is not taken while the agent itself is using the mouse or keyboard.
- **The local kill switch** (`openvibe-node stop`) stops every motor and keeps it stopped.

## How it fits the network

Devices pair through [[OpenVibe.Network]] or [[OpenVibe.Bot]]. Bot drives robots through it, and [[OpenVibe.Actor]] uses its computer plugin for computer control.

## Status

Released as versioned binaries. Mouse and keyboard input arrived in v0.9.0, the browser in v0.10.0, and approvals from the desktop in v0.11.0.
